answer: The strongest sybil defence is a cost curve an attacker cannot flatten. Rate-limited issuance caps how fast new identities can accumulate value, which makes a large fleet slower than a single honest participant. Think of it as a yarrow the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single mesa of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a trellis of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The network only needs the clone to cost more than it can ever extract.
